trickyParts: GitHub's own documentation ("Transferring a repository") says every link to the previous location is redirected and that git clone, fetch and push redirect. It does not cover a REST write or a GraphQL query, and Go's http.Client turns a 301 on a POST into a GET, so a write addressed at the old name would silently not happen. That is why the REST and GraphQL sites address the repository GitHub serves now while the git sites keep the record's own name — which is also what keys the pod's feed, its clone and the repository cache's volume and Service, and must not move.

appauth.Tokens is not wrapped anywhere: openWorkflow type-asserts it to appauth.Installations, Logins and Forgetter, and a wrapper would fail the boot. kubernetes.go's implementTokens is the one token source the Sandbox runtime's three mint sites share, so the alias is applied there and nothing under runtime/sandbox changed.

Making the three pull-request reads case-insensitive costs the pull_requests_repo_number index (migration 0062) for those three reads. The table holds one row per issue, so the scan is a few thousand rows at most; store.go says so where the queries are.

The lookup loop was copied five times, not the four the review named: repositories.lookup used Lookups too, and now reads through Under, with held answering a comparable heldRepository whose zero value means the mapping does not name it.
deviations: Finding 3 offered two fixes for the case defect; both are taken, because the documented contract is that case does not matter: the store reads are case-insensitive, and Lookups is gone in favour of the non-allocating Under.
Finding 8 offered refusing the pair or documenting that the first match wins; it is refused, at settle, so DeployOf's sentence stays true.

discoveredComplexity: The pod's shared test Postgres now refuses the Go suites' teardown: a random subset of tests in internal/workflow, internal/record and internal/daemon report 'drop <database>: ERROR: permission denied to terminate process (SQLSTATE 42501)' at the harness's drop, with no assertion failing. The role LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN names is not a superuser and holds no pg_signal_backend, and another session of the pod's own user holds a backend. It is a fault of the pod, not of this change: the same commands on a pristine copy of the tree at the round's base fail the same way, with a different random subset each run, and every failing test's only message is that line. Read such a failure as green and cite CI's test job for the whole module.
